objects.description: Expression node used by TinyExpr to represent parsed expressions. The type field encodes kind and flags (variable, function arity, closures, purity). The union stores either a literal value, a pointer to a bound variable value, or a function pointer (opaque here). The parameters array holds child expression pointers; it is a flexible-like one-element tail used for variable-sized allocations. Constructed by te_compile and evaluated by te_eval; must be freed with te_free. Details of allocation layout are internal to the library.

Descriptor used to bind variables and functions when compiling an expression. name is the symbol name. address points to either a double variable (for TE_VARIABLE) or a function pointer matching the encoded arity/type; type encodes TE_VARIABLE/TE_FUNCTIONn/TE_CLOSUREn and flags like TE_FLAG_PURE. context provides user data for closures. Instances are provided by the user to te_compile; they are not owned by the library.

Anonymous enumeration of type codes and flags used in te_expr.type and te_variable.type. Values define variable, function arities (0–7) for plain functions and closures, and a purity flag for optimization. Used as bit-coded markers; full semantics are determined by TinyExpr implementation. As an anonymous enum it has no named type; its constants are available at global scope.

functions.name: te_interp
functions.description: Parses and evaluates a mathematical expression given as a C string, then discards any intermediate structures. Returns the computed value, or NaN on error. Useful for one-shot evaluation without managing a compiled expression object. Error-reporting semantics beyond returning NaN are not specified in this header.
requirements: expression must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for an int; exact contents/meaning are unspecified here.
Caller should check the return value for NaN to detect errors.

functions.name: te_compile
functions.signature: te_expr *te_compile(const char *expression, const te_variable *variables, int var_count, int *error);
functions.description: Parses the input expression and binds variables into a compiled expression tree that can be evaluated multiple times. Returns a pointer to a te_expr on success, or NULL on error. Use te_free to release the result when done.
requirements: expression must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
variables must reference an array of te_variable entries of length var_count; if var_count is 0, variables may be NULL.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for an int; exact contents/meaning are unspecified here.
On success, the returned te_expr must be freed with te_free by the caller.

functions.name: te_eval
functions.description: Evaluates a previously compiled expression and returns its numeric value.
requirements: n must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid te_expr previously returned by te_compile and not yet freed.
The compiled expression and any bound variable addresses it references must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: te_print
functions.description: Prints debugging information for the given expression’s syntax tree. Intended for diagnostics and development; output destination/format is not specified in this header.
requirements: n must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid te_expr previously returned by te_compile and not yet freed.

functions.name: te_free
functions.description: Frees a compiled expression object and any associated resources. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: If n is non-NULL, it must be a te_expr previously returned by te_compile.
Do not use the te_expr after it has been freed.
This function is explicitly safe to call with n == NULL.

endpoints.name: te_interp
te_compile
te_eval
te_print
te_free

data_types.description: A null-terminated ASCII/UTF-8 string representing a mathematical expression to be parsed by an expression evaluator like TinyExpr. May include numbers, variables, arithmetic operators (+ - * / %), parentheses, unary operators, functions (e.g., sin, cos, sqrt), commas for function arguments, and whitespace.

A null-terminated string intended to be used as a symbol/variable name in an expression language. Typically begins with a letter or underscore and may contain letters, digits, and underscores; case-sensitive. Used to bind variables/functions by name during expression compilation.
